name: Advision Cache Management
note: Documentation of what this plugin leaves on a site, for whoever writes a scanner rule or a Hawkeye mute. It is not a trust anchor: nothing should be exempted because this file says so. Verify the plugin directory against the release's checksums.sha256 first.

files.changes_on: self-update from this repository's GitHub releases

cron_events.why: runs the next step of a background clear: after a mode's pause, after a warm-up hands back a cursor, or after a fatal ended the request mid-step

options.name: advcm_jobs
options.why: the last 10 clears (up to 30 while waiting for Hawkeye)

options.name: advcm_layers
options.why: per layer, when it was last cleared and how

options.name: advcm_lock_<job id>
options.why: one row while a job is running; deleted when it stops

options.name: advcm_last_error
options.why: the last fault the plugin's guards caught, shown on its screen for a day

wordpress_own_names_touched.name: update_plugins
wordpress_own_names_touched.why: so the Plugins screen re-reads the update list after a release check, as WordPress does after an update

transients.name: advcm_release
transients.why: the updater's cached answer from GitHub

transients.name: advcm_notice_<user id>
transients.why: a one-minute message after a refused press

capability_mechanism: a user_has_cap filter that only adds advcm_* keys; never written to roles or user meta

outbound_requests.why: update check, at most every 12 hours
the update package, through WordPress's own upgrader
